description: FlareNova turns satellite fire data into a clearer picture of our planet. By harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS hotspot observations, we uncover where, when, and how burning activity changes over time. We combine NASA Earth data, smart analysis, and interactive visualization to transform complex fire observations into meaningful insights for a better understanding of our planet.

Project Summary

ASTRAVITALL is an autonomous, Earth-independent astronaut health monitoring and clinical decision support platform designed for deep-space exploration missions. Built with FastAPI and a React cyber-metallic interface, it integrates real-time telemetry across vital signs, sleep cycles, radiation dosimetry (GCR/SPE), exercise countermeasures, cognitive readiness, and mental health check-ins.

The system addresses the challenge of deep-space communication latency—where real-time consultation with Earth-based flight surgeons is impossible. ASTRAVITALL bridges this critical gap through onboard automated anomaly detection against NASA-STD-3001 clinical standards, an interactive 3D holographic neurological scanner, a multi-organ anatomical status model, encrypted mission diary logging, and automated generation of tamper-evident clinical PDF health dossiers with cryptographic SHA-256 verification.

Autonomous health oversight is paramount for human survival on long-duration journeys like Artemis and crewed Mars missions. By transforming disparate biomedical telemetry into actionable clinical intelligence directly aboard the spacecraft, ASTRAVITALL empowers astronauts to detect microgravity-induced physiological degradation early, safeguard crew operational performance, and preserve human life without relying on continuous ground control intervention.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

ASTRAVITALL is an Earth-independent medical operations (EIMO) platform designed to monitor, analyze, and protect the health of astronaut crews during long-duration deep-space missions.

  • Multi-Stream Telemetry Ingestion: Aggregates physiological metrics (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, body temperature, respiratory rate), environmental radiation dosimetry (Galactic Cosmic Rays and Solar Particle Events), sleep architecture, physical countermeasure compliance (ARED resistive/T2 aerobic training), and cognitive vigilance scores.
  • Autonomous Anomaly Detection Engine: Continuously benchmarks live telemetry against established spaceflight medical thresholds (NASA-STD-3001) using algorithmic screening to identify physiological deterioration before it escalates into a medical emergency.
  • Interactive Diagnostic Interfaces: Features an interactive 3D anatomy viewer and a holographic 3D rotating neuro-scanner rendering dynamic cross-sectional cranial slices and biomarker metrics.
  • Clinical Health Dossiers & Mission Logging: Generates certified medical evaluation reports (Physical Health, Pre-EVA clearance, Neurological, Dosimetry) downloadable as tamper-evident PDFs with cryptographic SHA-256 validation, accompanied by an encrypted mission diary for crew reflections and operational logging.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero-Latency Clinical Autonomy: Fully functional locally onboard the spacecraft, resolving the up to 22-minute light-speed communication delay between Earth and Mars.
  • Holistic Health Triad: Unifies physical vitals, psychological well-being (mood and stress journaling), and cognitive readiness into a single cohesive interface.
  • Early Preventative Intervention: Displays normal baseline reference ranges beneath every physiological attribute, enabling instant deviation recognition.
  • Crew Compliance Tracking: Directly tracks daily microgravity countermeasure protocols (resistive and aerobic exercise) to combat bone density loss, cardiovascular deconditioning, and muscle atrophy.
  • Verifiable Medical Provenance: Cryptographically seals clinical reports with SHA-256 digital signatures, ensuring data integrity across flight surgeon reviews and post-mission epidemiology.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to enable sustainable human life beyond low Earth orbit. On missions to the Moon, Mars, and deep space, astronauts cannot abort to Earth or await real-time advice during acute medical scenarios. ASTRAVITALL bridges the gap between mission control and the autonomous spacecraft, reducing mission-critical health risks, preventing preventable medical aborts, and providing astronauts with the medical self-sufficiency required to explore the solar system safely.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend:
    • Languages & Core: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3
    • Framework & Build: React 18, Vite
    • Styling & Design: Tailwind CSS (cyber-metallic glassmorphism aesthetic)
    • Data Visualization & Graphics: HTML5 Canvas (3D rotating wireframe/particle scanner), Recharts, Lucide React icons
    • Language: Python 3.11+
    • Web Framework: FastAPI (high-throughput asynchronous REST APIs)
    • Database & ORM: SQLite, SQLAlchemy
    • Data & Machine Learning: NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn
    • Document Generation: ReportLab (vectorized clinical PDF generation engine)
    • Git, GitHub, Uvicorn ASGI server
    • Cloudflare Edge Tunneling (TLS/HTTPS end-to-end encryption)
    • JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication architecture

5. How is your project creative?

  • Cyber-Metallic "Liquid Spacecraft" Aesthetic: Replaces intimidating hospital charts with a sleek, mission-grade dark UI featuring brushed metallic tones, frosted glassmorphism cards, and liquid neon status accents engineered for low eye-strain in dimly lit spacecraft modules.
  • Holographic 3D Neuro Scanner: Features an interactive 3D spatial brain model that crews can rotate and inspect alongside synchronized CT cross-sectional scans, laser sweep diagnostics, and reaction-time metrics.
  • Interactive Anatomy Mapping: Astronauts can visually inspect localized organ and musculoskeletal statuses on an intuitive interactive body diagram rather than deciphering raw numerical tables.
  • Dual Mission Diary: Combines clinical telemedicine logging with an encrypted personal astronaut journal—acknowledging that psychological decompression is just as vital as physical maintenance.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Communication Latency & Offline-First Reliability: Deep-space missions cannot rely on cloud servers or ground-based APIs. The entire platform was designed with a local-first architecture capable of running 100% offline aboard spacecraft computing hardware.
  • NASA Medical Standards Compliance: Data thresholds, countermeasure targets, and vital ranges were modeled around NASA-STD-3001 (Space Flight Human-System Standard) and the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Evidence Books.
  • Cognitive Load & Alarm Fatigue: Spaceflight environments are high-stress. The UI organizes alerts into clean severity hierarchies (Normal, Attention, Critical) with explicit normal range indicators so crews can assess status at a single glance without information overload.
  • Data Integrity & Confidentiality: Implemented multi-tier privacy levels for crew logs and SHA-256 hashing on exported medical dossiers to maintain clinical chain-of-custody.
